SSD bay insertion test actuator · CATIA V5

Designed a compact two-cylinder pneumatic actuator in CATIA V5 to drive SSD bay insertion and removal testing: a housing with two parallel Ø9.53 mm bores, a mounting plate, and a Ø6.35 mm rod piston with three lands and two seal grooves.

Each part has a full drawing to ASME Y14.5-2018 with GD&T and ASME B4.2 fits: H9 bores against e8 piston lands, and an h6 rod into an H7 mount bore. Seal grooves follow the McMaster-Carr 9691K111 specification, and the housing has SAE J1926-1 size -4 plug ports plus M5 ports for off-the-shelf fittings.

Design for manufacturing is in the drawings: both cylinders bored in one setup, finishes called out per surface (Ra 0.4 µm in the bores), and anodize masking for threads and close-fit bores. All parts are 6061-T6.

AME 508 final project · Team of three

Trained a Deep Operator Network to predict the outlet temperature profile of the Formula SAE Electric battery cold plate from inlet velocity and inlet temperature, replacing a full CFD run for each operating point.

Training data came from 65 ANSYS Fluent simulations: 13 inlet velocities (0.004 to 0.01 m/s) by 5 inlet temperatures (308 to 328 K). Both the branch and trunk networks are MLPs. The final model was chosen after 23 rounds of manual hyperparameter tuning, with multiple runs per setting to handle stochastic variation and higher Adam betas to stop loss overshoot.

My part: generating the Fluent simulation data and training the network.

Result: 0.12 K average deviation, 0.6% maximum error, 0.04% validation error.
